text:
maria: FYI I'm hitting runtime failures when calling the Redwood JS SDK from Next.js middleware (edge). error: `ReferenceError: require is not defined` then after switching imports `TypeError: globalThis.crypto.subtle is undefined`.
kevin: middleware is ESM on edge, so CJS `require` will blow up. are you pulling the CJS package by accident?
sam: paste your import line? bundlers sometimes pick wrong entry.
maria: I had `const { createClient } = require('@redwood/inference')` inside `middleware.ts`  facepalm. switching to `import` helped but then the crypto issue appeared.
leo: import the edge entry: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'`. the edge build uses WebCrypto only.
maria: did that, plus `export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }`, but `crypto.subtle` is still undefined in both `next dev` and preview.
kevin: Next edge runtimes vary. Vercel preview exposes WebCrypto usually, but local dev can be missing. also some regions/runtimes differ.
sam: short-term dev workaround: guard for `globalThis.crypto?.subtle` and use a dev shim for signing. but we shouldn't rely on that for preview/prod.
maria: stack trace points to `auth/signature.ts` in the SDK. I tried a local change: prefer `globalThis.crypto.subtle` if present, else use `await import('crypto').then(m => m.webcrypto.subtle)`. but dynamic Node import doesn't work on edge.
leo: exactly. the SDK should not attempt node:crypto in edge builds at all. we need clear, separate build entries: node (cjs), module (esm/node), and edge (pure web). we ship an `/edge` entry but Next's resolver sometimes collapses exports.
kevin: action: update package exports to make edge unambiguous. add conditional exports like \"exports\": {\"./edge\": {\"import\": \"./dist/edge/index.mjs\"}, \".\": {\"node\": {...}, \"default\": \"...\"}}. also add a `browser`/`edge` conditional.
sam: recommend adding a runtime assertion in each build: edge build should assert presence of `globalThis.crypto?.subtle` and throw early if missing, node build should assert `typeof process !== 'undefined'` and presence of node crypto. that fails fast and improves DX.
maria: local workaround that worked: created `lib/redwood-edge-client.ts` in my app with `export { createClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` and imported that from middleware. preview started to behave.
leo: good pragmatic fix. we'll add a sample `next-middleware` example repo showing the explicit edge import. docs should show three import patterns: `@redwood/inference/edge` (middleware/edge), `@redwood/inference` (server/node), and `@redwood/inference/node` (explicit node).
kevin: also watch for other Web APIs differences: `AbortSignal`, response streaming (`body.getReader()`), and `Request`/`Response` shapes. add small compatibility helpers in SDK: `safeGetReader(response)` and `ensureAbortController()`.
sam: I'll open a PR: 1) strengthen package exports, 2) add runtime guards and clearer error messages, 3) doc snippets for Next middleware and a minimal sample repo, 4) tests that bundle example in Next to catch regressions.
leo: deploy-bot: create branch `edge-import-guards` and run CI.
deploy-bot: patch branch `edge-import-guards` created; CI queued.
maria: thanks all, saved me hours. will delete my local adapter once the PR lands. :tada:
